Let me think about the game design: "Tower defense upgrade game with 1 tower but multiple tower replacement types". Interesting concept: a single fixed tower slot. You upgrade it, and can replace the tower type (each type has different attack pattern), losing or keeping some upgrade levels. Multiple replacement types. Build canvas game, single HTML file ideally, no build step. Use plain JS, maybe split files? Simpler: index.html + game.js + styles.css. Ensure it runs via node default server on 3002.

Feature set:
- Path with enemies, waves.
- One central tower (or one tower slot) on the map; tower types: e.g. Arrow (fast single target), Cannon (splash), Frost (slow), Laser/Beam (continuous), Tesla/Chain (chain lightning), Sniper (long range high damage). All at a fixed build pad? "1 tower but multiple tower replacement types" — one tower, can swap its type. Upgrade levels persist? Design choice: swapping type resets type-specific? Better: upgrades are shared "tower core level"; each type scales; replacing costs a swap fee and keeps core level? To make replacement meaningful and tactical, keep core level (upgrades) across replacements, but replacing costs coins and has a short cooldown. Maybe each type has own upgrade track? The phrase "tower defense upgrade game with 1 tower but multiple tower replacement types" suggests one tower that can be replaced with different types. Upgrading probably global tower level, and swapping types changes behavior.

Alternative more interesting: the single tower can be "reforged" into different classes mid-wave, upgrade levels persist but each replacement type has different stats and unique ability. Since there's only one tower, difficulty balanced.

Let me design polished visuals: Canvas 2D, neon sci-fi. Map with winding path. Single tower at center? Path around center so tower in middle can shoot all around. One tower at map center, enemies follow a winding loop around it. Range circle visible. Drag? No, no placement since one tower.

- Start with 300 gold, 20 lives.
- Waves spawn enemies along path. Enemy types: grunt, runner, tank, shield, healer? boss.
- Tower types:
  1. Pulse (basic, fast single target) — starting.
  2. Cannon (splash damage, slow).
  3. Frost (slows enemies, low damage, AoE slow aura or projectile).
  4. Tesla (chain lightning).
  5. Sniper (long range, high single damage, slow).
  6. Flamer? (cone/DoT). Maybe 6 types total.
- Each type has stats scaled by tower level.
- Upgrades: damage/rate/range? Simpler: global "Core Level" with costs escalating; upgrade button. Also type-specific? Maybe global upgrades: Power (damage +15% each), Cadence (fire rate), Reach (range) each upgradeable separately to level 5. But with replacement types, the upgrade strategy interacts. Hmm, maybe simpler and more legible: single "Level" upgrade boosts all stats, and "Overclock" temp ability? Let's keep upgrade clear: tower level 1-10, increasing damage/range/rate. Swap types costs gold and resets nothing? It keeps level. This makes an interesting decision: choose type for wave composition.

Need ability to target priority: First/Last/Strong/Close. Nice.

- Selling? No, one tower; maybe not.
- Swap cost varies by type. Types unlock progressively by wave? Unlock system adds progression: types unlocked at waves 2,4,6,8,10? Could be all available but costs. Maybe unlocking makes progression. User asked multiple tower replacement types, so make all visible from the start, with affordable costs; some locked until wave N for progression flavor? I'd avoid locking core feature; but tiered unlock with clear labels can be good. Let's do all types available from start; costs vary 60-180, so early choices matter. Add a "REFORGE" grid of six buttons, showing stats.

- Enemy kills give gold. Wave clear bonus. Waves endless with escalating difficulty, bosses every 5 waves. Score. Win condition? Endless with high score, game over when lives 0. Maybe show "best wave" persisted in localStorage.

- Game states: menu, playing, paused, gameover.
- Start wave button; auto wave start maybe timer with skip bonus? Classic: "Send next wave early for bonus". Allow starting waves early with gold bonus based on remaining time? Let's keep simple: waves auto-start after delay, with a "Start Wave" button for early bonus.

Single HTML? Better structure: index.html, styles.css, game.js. Also package? A server script? The runtime default-start may serve static on 3002. Need figure out how default server works. The start.sh uses RUNTIME_DIR scripts/default-start.mjs. Check env and .agents README.

# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │

import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')
      res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache')
      const content = readFileSync(file)
      if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') {
        const html = content.toString()
        res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}</body>`) : html + livePreviewScript)
      } else res.end(content)
    } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') }
  })
  server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() })
  server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0')
  return server
}
if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) await start()

Wow forms wildly imbalanced:
- Pulse wins with 17 lives (after rebalance). Cryo & Blaze win 20 lives easily.
- Mortar and tesla barely win.
- Rail loses at 14! Rail is supposed boss killer but piercing line may miss and single-target low; also it cannot handle groups. Its DPS 223 max is lower than pulse 354. Rail needs a buff. Cryo surprisingly strong despite low DPS because 30% amp + slow; apparently enough. Blaze super strong (cone + long-ish range 284 at max) and burn.
- Mortar weak: splash damage perhaps misses moving targets (prediction based on current speed fine) but travel 0.72s; damage 36/1.35=26.7; at max 177 single, splash 66 radius maybe hits 2-3. Needs buff. Also its range 330+99=429, so good coverage. But 4 lives at end. Could increase damage or splash.
- Tesla weak: 5 lives. Chain damage 18/0.85=21; max 141 per target ×2.57=362 total; good but chain only 5 targets at level 10; late waves 24 enemies, but total. Maybe needs buff.
- Pulse too strong? It won 17 lives now (with leaks at 17-19 but survived). Good baseline.
- Cryo/Blaze too strong, both 20. Blaze's 20 due to high DPS 356 at max (single) + cone multi + burn, and range 284. Maybe burn stacking too strong? Burn DPS 7*3.97=27.8 for 2.4s, stacking refresh; at 7.14 ticks/s, every tick refreshes, so burn always ~27.8 DPS extra. Not huge. Cone hits multiple.
- Cryo 20 lives due to 30% amp and slow, low damage but targets spend longer in range. Maybe slow + amp strong. It doesn't need nerf necessarily; high skill/utility. But pulse should be baseline, cryo 20 maybe okay if it's satisfying. However game should challenge. Need overall difficulty bump so not everything maxed wins easily, but ensure all forms viable with good play. Maybe add late-wave difficulty more and buff weak forms.

The issue: late game max level 10 reached around wave 17-19 (except cryo/blaze at 17). Still wins. Could increase late HP again (wave 17+). Maybe specific ramp: hpMul with cubic term. Or add more enemies. Need challenge; but also only one tower so difficulty should be manageable.

We need to keep forms distinct:
- Pulse: single target, reliable.
- Mortar: splash, should be strong vs groups but weak vs single.
- Cryo: control + amp, lower DPS.
- Blaze: short-range high DPS.
- Tesla: chain, strong vs clustered, weaker vs single.
- Rail: long-range pierce, strong vs bosses/lines, weak vs spread.

Current path lanes are separated such that groups may be spread along lane, so splash/chain less effective. Mortar/tesla underperform because groups spread over 30px? Enemies spawn 0.5s apart at speed 92 → 46px spacing. Splash 66 can hit 2; chain range 122. Should be okay.
- Rail piercing line only hits enemies aligned along the shot line; enemies in a lane are spaced along same lane, and the tower shoots at one target. If targeting "first", the line from tower to target may pass through some, but not all; path is horizontal lane, tower center; line to target crosses lane at angle, likely only target. So pierce rarely hits more than 1. Its single DPS is low (223), so bad. Need rail to be stronger single-target plus pierce. Raise damage significantly (e.g., 105 base) and/or rate. It's the boss killer; should be comparable single-target. Let's set rail damage 95, interval 2.0, range 430. Max DPS = 95/2.0=47.5 ×3.97×1.675=316 single. Still below pulse 354 but pierce bonus. Boss value. Also maybe ignores slow? no. Add charge .5. Good.
- Mortar: increase base damage to 48 (36→48), splash 76, interval 1.3. Max DPS single 48/1.3=36.9×6.65=245; splash 2-3→500-735. Good. Also direct hits? Full damage in splash. Should be strong.
- Tesla: increase damage to 22, interval .8, chain falloff .88, chain range 135. Max per-target 22/.8=27.5×6.65=183; chain 4 at lvl10? chains = 3 + floor(9/3)=6. Total multiplier 1+0.88+... 5 terms = 1+0.88+0.774+0.681+0.599+0.527=4.46 → 816 AoE. Strong. Maybe too strong. Current chains 3+3=6 too. Damage 18→21, interval .8, chainRange 130. Fine.
- Blaze: maybe shorten range to 175 and reduce burn? It already has 20 lives; but other forms need buffs. Keep or slight nerf: damage 7.5→7, burn 6. But short range. It should be great when upgraded. With max range 284, quite long for a flamethrower; maybe range 170 + 11*9=269. Still. Could reduce range growth for all? leave.
- Cryo: fine; maybe 20 lives is okay as control.
- Pulse: maybe base 16→15 to keep baseline; with difficulty bump should drop lives. But pulse should be viable. Keep 16, maybe early analytics.

Game difficulty: Max cryo/blaze won 20 lives; need bump late waves. Increase hpMul late with cubic? Let's do a `lateRamp` factor: hpMul = 1 + 0.16*(n-1) + 0.008*(n-1)^2 (w20 1+3.04+2.888=6.93; +15% over current 6.02). Count 30. Boss 900*(1+0.30*(n-5)) → w20 4950. This adds ~15%. Pulse maybe leaks more; pulse-only might lose around 19 but that's okay? We want skilled players to win. The auto policy isn't skilled (max pulse) and lost at 19 before... wait after rebalance pulse-only fixed form won 17 lives. The earlier sim2 with pulse only lost at 19. Why difference? sim2 upgraded during waves with same policy? Actually forms.json pulse run result: victory 17 lives, level 10, log shows leaks at wave 17 (2), wave 18 0? wave 19 1, wave 20 0. sim2 lost at 19 with 20 lives until 15, then 18,8,5,0. The difference: sim2 advanced in 1s chunks and upgraded during wave; forms run also. Maybe sim2 was before the config changes (hpMul etc.)? Yes sim2 was after changes? We changed config then ran sim2: pulse lost at wave 19. Then forms run pulse won. Difference: forms run did `n.start()` then started each wave; reforge pulse? no. Hmm sim2 had `let spent=0;` unused. Maybe upgrade decision during wave differs due to plus reserve? sim2 upgraded whenever affordable; forms same. Why different? Possibly game UI sync / RAF interference? Or randomness in wave composition (seed differs each start). Yes RNG seed varies per run; composition varies. So outcome varies. Fine.

Thus pulse can win or lose depending on RNG and upgrades. That's decent. But cryo/blaze win comfortably. Increase difficulty a bit and buff weak forms.

Could also make 20 waves requires more strategy by reducing max level to 8? Then max DPS lower. But upgrades to 10 feel good. Keep.

Need test "smart swap" after buffs. But the previous smart policy under-upgraded due to reserve; likely a human would upgrade more. We can craft a better strategy: focus on one primary form for most waves, swap situationally. The design should allow swapping but not require constant.

Maybe economy: raising upgrade costs made constant swapping underpowered. Fine; swaps should be tactical.

Need ensure all forms can win. After buffs, test again fixed forms. Let's apply:
- mortar damage 48, interval 1.3, splash 76.
- tesla damage 21, interval 0.8, chainRange 132, falloff .87.
- rail damage 96, interval 2.05, range 430, charge 0.5, pierce 16.
- blaze maybe keep.
- difficulty hpMul 0.16/0.007 (w20=1+3.04+2.527=6.567), count cap 30. Boss 0.30 -> 4950.
Let's calculate w20 regular 24*80*6.57=12.6k + 4.95=17.6k. Pulse max 354 over ~36s =12.7k + some out of range time; fails. Maybe too hard for pulse. But pulse-only shouldn't necessarily win; however "pulse" is default and players who don't swap may lose final. That's the premise. But all forms perhaps should be able to win with good upgrades/targeting. Pulse at 17 lives under current difficulty; +10-15% could still win with leaks. Let's choose hpMul 0.15/0.0065: w20 = 1+2.85+2.347=6.197 (+3%). Boss 0.3 (4950 vs 4680 +6%). Mild bump. Buffed forms should handle.

Maybe also make wave 20 harder via final boss HP 5500 specifically: boss scaling 0.32 → 5220. Fine.

Let's apply buffs and slight difficulty.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable browser tower-defense upgrade game with exactly one tower that can be reforged into multiple tower types.
- The game must be built now without clarifying questions, with reasonable assumptions noted at completion.

## Requirements
- Tower defense game with upgrades and multiple tower replacement types, but only one active tower.
- Complete and playable in the browser, including win/lose/restart states.
- Responsive layout with usable mobile touch controls.
- No clarifying questions; briefly note assumptions when finished.

## Decisions
- Built a static vanilla HTML/CSS/JS canvas game named **NEXUS**, served directly from `index.html`; no build step or external assets.
- One central tower with six reforgeable forms: PULSE, MORTAR, CRYO, BLAZE, TESLA, RAIL. Reforging preserves the shared tower level, costs credits, has a 2.2s cooldown, and triggers 4s overdrive (+35% rate, +6% range).
- 20-wave campaign, boss every 5 waves, 20 starting integrity, 260 starting credits, level cap 10.
- Enemies: Drone, Runner, Brute, Aegis (shield), Splitter (spawns shards), bosses named GOLIATH, LEVIATHAN, OBLIVION, SINGULARITY.
- Added target priorities FIRST/LAST/STRONG/CLOSE, procedural WebAudio SFX, mute/speed/pause/help controls, keyboard shortcuts, persistent best wave/score, and a debug API at `window.__NEXUS__`.
- Mobile portrait uses a sticky stage while the panel scrolls beneath, so the arena remains visible while reforging.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project structure created: `index.html`, `styles.css`, `src/config.js`, `src/path.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/game.js`, `src/main.js`.
- Implemented full gameplay loop, all six tower behaviors, projectiles/beams/particles, status effects, waves, bosses, economy, scoring, overlays, help modal, and responsive UI.
- Added and verified server execution on port 3002 via tmux session `nexus`.
- Fixed favicon 404, faint track, tower position/range, exit portal clipping, mobile intro overflow, and mobile sticky-stage layout.
- Ran balance simulations; pulse-only / mortar / cryo / blaze / tesla / rail all win at least some configurations after buffing mortar, tesla, and rail. Rail was previously losing at wave 19 and now wins after buff.
- Verified desktop (1440×900), small desktop (1050×793), and mobile (390×844) layouts with screenshots.
- Verified Tesla chain lightning renders correctly by freezing game speed after beam spawn.

### Active
- Final visual/gameplay verification and polish, especially checking remaining tower forms’ effects (mortar, cryo, blaze, rail), pause/result/help overlays, and mobile interaction at real-time speed.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect screenshots for remaining forms/effects and overlays; fix any visual or functional defects.
2. Test real-time play (not only `advance`) for wave start, firing, leaks, wave clear, pause, restart, victory, and defeat.
3. Confirm no console errors other than resolved favicon; check all buttons and keyboard shortcuts.
4. Consider improving large empty lower arena area, if warranted.
5. Update `README.md` with game instructions, controls, and note assumptions.
6. Stop/clean up the tmux `nexus` server if needed, then summarize completion.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: page structure, HUD, overlays, help modal, panel markup.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: complete visual design and responsive/sticky mobile layout.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/config.js`: balance, tower forms, enemies, upgrade costs, wave generation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: game engine, combat, six tower mechanics, canvas rendering.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: DOM wiring, UI synchronization, input handling, debug API.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio sound effects.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/path.js`: rounded sampled enemy track.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`: project start script.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: verification screenshots.

## Important Context
- Server is running in tmux: `tmux new-session -d -s nexus 'cd /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround && PORT=3002 ./start.sh > /tmp/opencode/nexus-server.log 2>&1'`; URL `http://localhost:3002`.
- Playwright CLI is available; Chromium was installed with `playwright-cli install-browser chromium`. The browser is currently open at desktop size 1440×900, game paused via `game.speed=0`, mid-wave 15 with TESLA and visible lightning.
- Debug API: `window.__NEXUS__` exposes `start`, `startWave`, `upgrade`, `reforge`, `advance`, `getUI`, `sync`, `game`, `audio`.
- Balance sims return compact results via `n.advance(1)` loops; `game.advance(seconds)` bypasses normal RAF time.
- Key current balance constants: `UPGRADE_COSTS = [60,100,160,240,360,520,740,1000,1350]`; enemy `hpMul: 1 + 0.15*(wave-1) + 0.0065*(wave-1)^2`; boss HP `900*(1+0.3*(wave-5))`.
- Rail stats after buff: `damage:135`, `interval:2`, `range:430`, `charge:0.45`, `pierce:18`.
- All files are currently uncommitted/untracked; git status showed only the initial repository commit plus new files.
